title: Add public all-PDFs feed page aggregating uploads from all accounts

requirements.summary: Create a new publicly accessible '/feed' page that displays all PDFs from all users in a single feed, showing title, uploader principal (truncated), upload date, and an 'Open' button navigating to /view/<shareId>, sorted newest-first
acceptanceCriteria: A new route '/feed' (or '/all') renders the all-PDFs page without requiring login.
All PDFs from all uploaders are listed, fetched via the existing listPdfs() query hook.
Each card displays: PDF title, uploader principal (truncated), upload date, and an 'Open' button.
Clicking 'Open' navigates to /view/<shareId> for the correct PDF.
Entries are sorted newest-first by upload timestamp.
The page is linked from the site header/navigation.
The page matches the existing dark navy and amber visual theme (card layout, shadows, hover transitions).

file_operations.description: Create FeedPage component that fetches all PDFs via useListPdfs() from useQueries.ts, displays them in a grid of cards matching the GalleryPage card design (dark navy background, amber accents, hover transitions). Each card shows PDF title, truncated uploader principal (first 8 and last 4 characters), formatted upload date, and an 'Open' button that navigates to /view/{shareId}. Sort entries by uploadedAt timestamp descending. Display loading state while fetching. The page is publicly accessible (no authentication required). Match the visual theme from index.css (bg-background, card styling with shadows and borders).

requirements.summary: Add a 'Feed' navigation link in the site header that routes to the new all-PDFs feed page with active-route highlighting
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Feed' link appears in the top navigation bar alongside existing links.
The link routes to the new feed page.
The link is highlighted/active when the user is on the feed page.
No other navigation links are changed or removed.

file_operations.description: Add a new navigation link for 'Feed' in the navigation bar alongside the existing Gallery, Upload, and Dashboard links. The link should route to '/feed' and follow the same active-route highlighting pattern using the activeClass conditional styling (amber text color when active). Position it after the Gallery link and before Upload. Maintain the existing spacing and responsive layout of the nav links.

requirements.summary: Register the new '/feed' route in App.tsx to render FeedPage without authentication requirements
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating directly to '/feed' renders the FeedPage without a 404 or redirect.
The route is public (no auth guard).
All existing routes (/, /upload, /dashboard, /view/:shareId) continue to work unchanged.

file_operations.description: Register a new public route '/feed' in the TanStack Router configuration that renders the FeedPage component. Add the route alongside the existing public routes (Gallery, Viewer) without any authentication requirements. Import FeedPage from './pages/FeedPage'. Ensure the route does not conflict with existing routes and follows the same routing pattern as the GalleryPage route.
